ingredients.name: Cost
ingredients.note: Both platforms. Google 'Cost' = total spend for all interactions; Meta 'Amount spent' = approximate total spent, which Meta calls the numerator of every cost-per metric.

ingredients.name: Impressions
ingredients.note: Both platforms. Times an ad was shown. Meta counts an ad instance the first time it is on screen; both platforms leave out invalid traffic.

ingredients.name: Reach
ingredients.note: Both platforms, estimated and deduplicated. Meta counts Meta Accounts (sampled data). Google's 'Unique users' is modelled across devices and is only reported for Display, Video, Discovery (now Demand Gen) and App campaigns.

ingredients.name: Clicks
ingredients.note: Google only. Valid clicks on an ad; invalid clicks are filtered out of this column.

ingredients.name: Clicks (all)
ingredients.note: Meta only. Every click, tap or swipe on the ad: link clicks, profile clicks, reactions, comments, shares, media expands.

ingredients.name: Link clicks
ingredients.note: Meta only. Clicks on links in the ad that lead to the advertiser's chosen destination. A subset of Clicks (all).

ingredients.name: Unique link clicks
ingredients.note: Meta only. Number of Meta Accounts that made a link click (people, not actions). Estimated, sampled. It survived Meta's Oct 2024 removal of most unique metrics.

ingredients.name: Results
ingredients.note: Meta only. Outcomes that match the campaign's objective and settings, so what counts as a result changes per campaign. May be partly modelled.

ingredients.name: Purchases
ingredients.note: Meta only. Purchase events attributed to the ads (pixel, Conversions API, or purchases made on Meta surfaces).

ingredients.name: Leads
ingredients.note: Meta only. Leads attributed to the ads: instant forms, messaging leads and tracked off-Meta lead events.

ingredients.name: Purchases conversion value
ingredients.note: Meta only. Total value of attributed purchases. Purchases only, which makes it narrower than Google's Conv. value.

ingredients.name: ThruPlays
ingredients.note: Meta only. Video played to completion or for at least 15 seconds (97% of the length for shorter videos). A 6-second ThruPlay variant also exists.

ingredients.name: Post engagements
ingredients.note: Meta only. A bundle of actions on the ad post: reactions, comments, shares, saves, 3-second video plays, photo views, link clicks and more.

ingredients.name: Conversions
ingredients.note: Google only. Conversions from the primary conversion actions. Can be fractional because of attribution models, and may include modelled conversions.

ingredients.name: Conv. value
ingredients.note: Google only. Sum of the values of everything in the Conversions column, covering every primary conversion action and not just purchases.

ingredients.name: Interactions
ingredients.note: Google only. The main user action for each ad format: clicks for text, Shopping and image ads, TrueView views for video ads, engagements for some formats.

ingredients.name: Engagements
ingredients.note: Google only. Ad-format specific engagements, such as expanding a Lightbox or Gmail ad or watching a video ad for a set number of seconds. Not the same thing as Meta post engagements.

ingredients.name: TrueView views
ingredients.note: Google only. The billable YouTube view: 30 s or an interaction for in-stream ads; 10 s or a click for in-feed and Shorts ads (or the full ad if shorter). Different from Meta ThruPlays.

ingredients.name: Eligible impressions
ingredients.note: Google only. Google's estimate of the impressions the ads could have received, based on targeting, approval status and quality. It exists only inside impression-share formulas, not as a reportable column.

ingredients.name: Top impressions
ingredients.note: Google only (Search). Impressions shown among the top ads above organic results. Counts at most one impression per search, and is not a separate column.

ingredients.name: Absolute top impressions
ingredients.note: Google only (Search). Impressions in the very first ad slot among the top ads. Counts at most one impression per search, and is not a separate column.

ingredients.name: Invalid clicks
ingredients.note: Google only. Clicks Google classified as invalid (bots, accidental or fraudulent) and filtered out. They are not charged and not included in Clicks.

metrics.name: CPM (cost per 1,000 impressions)
metrics.definition: The average cost of 1,000 impressions, used to compare cost-efficiency across publishers and campaigns.

metrics.name: Cost per 1,000 Meta Accounts reached
metrics.definition: The average cost to reach 1,000 Meta Accounts. Like CPM, but divides by people reached instead of impressions. Estimated.
metrics.note: Meta's naming for the reach unit has changed over time (people, then Accounts Center accounts, now Meta Accounts). Google has no equivalent column.

metrics.name: Cost per click (all)
metrics.definition: The average cost of each click (all), where any click, tap or swipe on the ad counts.

metrics.name: CPC (cost per link click)
metrics.definition: The average cost of each link click, an industry benchmark for ad efficiency.
metrics.note: Link clicks are a subset of Clicks (all), so CPC (link) is always at least as high as CPC (all). Google's Avg. CPC divides by its own Clicks, which is neither Meta click type.

metrics.name: Cost per unique link click
metrics.definition: The average cost for each Meta Account that clicked a link. Estimated, from sampled data.
metrics.note: The Help Center page is titled 'Cost per unique click' but defines it with unique link clicks. Meta removed most 'cost per unique …' metrics on 30 Oct 2024; this one was not on the removal list.

metrics.name: CTR (all)
metrics.definition: The percentage of impressions where any click (all) happened.
metrics.note: Meta's page gives 'clicks (all) divided by impressions' and calls the result a percentage. The ×100 is how that percentage is displayed.

metrics.name: CTR (link click-through rate)
metrics.definition: The percentage of impressions that produced a link click, used to judge how well ads drive traffic.
metrics.note: Google has one CTR (Clicks ÷ Impressions). Meta splits CTR by click type.

metrics.name: Unique CTR (link click-through rate)
metrics.definition: The percentage of Meta Accounts that saw the ad and clicked a link. It counts accounts, not actions. Estimated, from sampled data.
metrics.note: A trap: the strainer is Reach, not Impressions. Both sides count people.

metrics.name: Frequency
metrics.definition: The average number of times each Meta Account saw the ad. Estimated, from sampled data.
metrics.note: Google's equivalent is 'Avg. impr. freq. / user'. Google's glossary term 'Frequency' means something else: the minimum number of times a user saw the ad.

metrics.name: Cost per result
metrics.definition: The average cost of each result, showing how cost-efficiently the campaign met its objective.
metrics.note: What a result is depends on the objective. Some results may be modelled, and for iOS 14+ the divisor is results reported by SKAdNetwork. Google's closest match is Cost / conv.

metrics.name: Result rate
metrics.definition: The percentage of impressions that produced a result.
metrics.note: This is the nearest Meta has to a conversion rate, but it divides by Impressions. Google's Conv. rate divides by Interactions.

metrics.name: Cost per purchase
metrics.definition: The average cost of each purchase attributed to the ads.
metrics.note: Channel-specific versions exist, such as cost per website purchase and cost per in-app purchase. Meta may not calculate this for iOS 14+ traffic.

metrics.name: Cost per lead
metrics.definition: The average cost of each lead attributed to the ads.

metrics.name: Cost per ThruPlay
metrics.definition: The average cost of each ThruPlay: a play to completion or of at least 15 seconds.
metrics.note: The page now labels this 'Cost per 15-second ThruPlay' and marks it as in development. A 'Cost per 6-second ThruPlay' also exists. Google's analogue, TrueView avg. CPV, uses a different view definition and only view-eligible cost.

metrics.name: Purchase ROAS (return on ad spend)
metrics.definition: The total return on ad spend from purchases attributed to the ads.
metrics.note: Cost moves to the strainer here. The result is a plain ratio (e.g. 3.2), not a percentage. It counts purchases only, while Google's Conv. value / cost counts every primary conversion action. Website and in-app ROAS variants exist.

metrics.name: Average purchases conversion value
metrics.definition: The average value of a purchase attributed to the ads; Meta's version of average order value.
metrics.note: Google's official 'Average order value' is Revenue ÷ Orders and needs cart data. Its general-purpose analogue is Value / conv.

metrics.name: Cost per post engagement
metrics.definition: The average cost of each post engagement, meaning any action on the ad post.
metrics.note: Post engagements bundle many action types, so they are not the same as Google's Engagements. Meta has no official 'engagement rate' column; its 'engagement rate ranking' is a diagnostic ranking, not a formula.

metrics.name: Average cost-per-thousand impressions
metrics.definition: The average amount charged per 1,000 impressions of the ad.
metrics.note: Derived from the written description; Google Help gives no explicit equation. Google words it as 'if you're using CPM bidding', and whether the column covers only CPM-bid traffic is UNVERIFIED. Same idea as Meta's CPM.

metrics.name: Average cost-per-click
metrics.definition: The average amount charged for a click: total cost of clicks divided by total clicks.
metrics.note: Strictly, the pot is the cost of clicks. On campaigns where every interaction is a click (e.g. Search), that equals Cost.

metrics.name: Clickthrough rate
metrics.definition: How often people who see the ad (or free listing) click it.

metrics.name: Average cost (per interaction)
metrics.definition: The average amount paid per interaction, whatever the main action for that ad format is.
metrics.note: A cross-campaign metric: an interaction is a click on Search and a TrueView view on video. Meta has no interaction concept.

metrics.name: Interaction rate
metrics.definition: How often people interact with the ad after it is shown.

metrics.name: Conversion rate
metrics.definition: The average number of conversions per ad interaction, shown as a percentage.
metrics.note: The strainer is Interactions, not Clicks, and only interactions that can be tracked to a conversion. It can go above 100% when several conversions are counted per interaction.

metrics.name: Cost per conversion
metrics.definition: How much each conversion cost on average.
metrics.note: Google's glossary calls this 'Average CPA'. Only the cost of conversion-trackable interactions goes in the pot. Meta's nearest equivalent is Cost per result.

metrics.name: Conversion value per cost
metrics.definition: Estimates return on investment: total conversion value divided by the total cost of all interactions.
metrics.note: This is Google's ROAS, although the column isn't called ROAS; Target ROAS bidding targets it. Google's separate 'ROI' is profit-based. Unlike Meta's Purchase ROAS, it counts every primary conversion action.

metrics.name: Value per conversion
metrics.definition: Roughly how much each conversion is worth on average.
metrics.note: The closest Google match to Meta's Average purchases conversion value.

metrics.name: TrueView average cost-per-view
metrics.definition: The average amount paid each time someone watches enough of a video ad to count as a TrueView view.
metrics.note: The Help Center only describes CPV bidding; the equation was taken from Google's own Ads API field definition. Only cost that was eligible for TrueView views goes in the pot (bumper and non-skippable ads are excluded). Formerly just 'Avg. CPV'.

metrics.name: TrueView view rate
metrics.definition: The percentage of video ad impressions that became a TrueView view.
metrics.note: Tricky definition: only impressions eligible for views count, so bumper and non-skippable impressions are excluded from the strainer. Formerly 'View rate' or 'VTR'. Separate in-stream, in-feed and Shorts rates exist.

metrics.name: Engagement rate
metrics.definition: How often people engage with the ad, per impression.
metrics.note: Meta has no official engagement-rate column.

metrics.name: Average cost-per-engagement
metrics.definition: The average amount charged for an ad engagement.
metrics.note: The Help Center only describes this metric in words; the equation matches the Google Ads API definition (total cost of engagements ÷ engagements). Strictly, the pot is the cost of engagements only.

metrics.name: Search impression share
metrics.definition: Impressions received on the Search Network divided by the estimated number of impressions the ads were eligible for.
metrics.note: Tricky: the strainer is Google's estimate, not a reportable count, and only Search Network impressions go in the pot. Values below 10% are reported as just under 10% (the API returns 0.0999). Meta has no impression share.

metrics.name: Search top impression rate
metrics.definition: The percentage of your Search ad impressions shown among the top ads above organic results.
metrics.note: The Help page's written equation divides by 'eligible impressions', but that contradicts its own definition ('percent of your ad impressions') and the Google Ads API. This uses the definition. Both sides count at most one impression per search, so the strainer is slightly smaller than the Impressions column.

metrics.name: Search absolute top impression rate
metrics.definition: The percentage of your Search ad impressions shown as the very first ad among the top ads.
metrics.note: Both sides count at most one (the most prominent) impression per search. Not the same as Search abs. top IS, which divides by eligible top impressions.

metrics.name: Invalid click rate
metrics.definition: The percentage of clicks that were classified as invalid and automatically filtered out.
metrics.note: The strainer items add up: Clicks + Invalid clicks, the filtered and unfiltered total, per the Google Ads API. This is needed because the Clicks column already excludes invalid clicks. The Help Center only says 'percentage of clicks'. Meta has no invalid-click column.

metrics.name: Average impression frequency per user
metrics.definition: The average number of times a unique user saw the ad during the period.
metrics.note: The Help page gives this equation for the 7- and 30-day versions; the plain column's equation is derived from its description. Only reported for Display, Video, Discovery (now Demand Gen) and App campaigns. It can't be summed across rows. Same recipe as Meta's Frequency.
